To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed the world's first 56 mm aperture dipole model magnet with a high field of 8 T and a high current density of 100 A/mm/sup 2/.
a 56 mm single-aperture superconducting model dipole magnet, which has the same specifications as the LHC dipole, was successfully developed and the magnet showed almost no quench training at 4K.
a 56 mm single dipole magnet with a central field of more than 9 T was developed and the first quench current reached 91% of that of the short sample.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the 56 mm single-aperture superconducting dipol model magnet for LCH.

the development of a 56mm single aperture superconductivity dipole model magnet which will be used as the framework of the LHC magnet R and D collaboration between KEK, CERN and the other institutes.
